newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Zastava mulls deal with France's Peugeot.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Zastava mulls deal with France's Peugeot.

text.p: Yugoslavia's car manufacturer Zastava could soon strike a deal with a foreign partner which industry analysts said on Monday was cruical for revival of car plant's production.
"The talks with a foreign partner entered final stage and signing a deal is only a matter of days," one Zastava Group official who asked not to be named told Reuters.
Belgrade media said French automobile producer Peugeot might be the new partner, but Zastava Group Executive Director Srboljub Vasovic neither confirmed nor denied the reports.
"The name of Zastava's foreign partner for complex cooperation in car production will soon be known," Vasovic was quoted by the local Tanjug newsagency as saying.
Zastava, producer of the small compact car Yugo, has been reported to be in talks with potential foreign partners for more than two years now.
South Korea's Hyundai Motor Company, Italy's Fiat SpA and France's PSA Peugeot Citroen were the three companies mentioned as potential partners.
The company, hit by the violent break-up of former Yugoslavia, war-related 1992-96 U.N. sanctions and mismanagement, suffers from chronic shortage of cash like the entire economy.

Industry sources saw foreign partner as the only possible way to secure funds needed for development and modernisation of production at the car plant. Yugo Florida, Zastava's latest model, was launched in 1988.
"The state with empty coffers and blocked access to international credits simply has no money to finance such an expensive industry like car production," said one analyst.
Production in Zastava, once main hard currency earner in the old Balkan federation, dropped to barely 10,000 vehicles in 1996 from its record high of 230,000 cars in 1989.
This year's plan was set at 22,500 cars out of which half should be exported.

As the production in the first three months was almost at a standstill, the Serbian government in April said it would secure an initial financial injection of 70.2 million dinars ($11.6 million) to kick-start this year's production.
The Group's spokesman Zvonko Osrecki said the factory, despite promised help, had difficulties in securing enough engines and parts from sub-contractors and financing production.
"Late government payments effected the production which is well below the plan," he said.
This year's to date production stands at 3,752 cars, of which 848 were produced in June, 1,001 in May and 747 in April.
"We expect July production to reach at least 1,400 cars. In August, our target is 3,000 cars," said Dragoslav Milosevic, of the car plant's production sector.
Analysts believed it would be better for the company to replace the manufacturing with the simple assembly of foreign automobiles.
But according to Vasovic, Zastava's main interests were to produce, sell and stay alive.

A source close to Zastava's negotiating team said a possible deal with Peugeot envisages both production of cars and spare parts. "Production of new model in Zastava car plant is planned for the next stage," the source said. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 311 4254
($1=6.0657 Yugoslav dinars)
